answer: No, your records do not show a blood clot in your lung. The scan you are remembering was most likely a CT angiography of your chest on 8 July 2025, a scan done to look for a pulmonary embolism (a blood clot in the lung). The report from that scan says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. It did note mild wear-and-tear changes in the thoracic (mid-back) spine. Pulmonary embolism was listed as a possible condition that day and was later marked as ruled out. The same day, a blood test called D-dimer was raised (0.92 mg/L FEU). A raised D-dimer does not by itself mean there is a clot, since it can rise for many reasons, and the scan is what checked for one. Your records have no later diagnosis of a lung clot up to 30 October 2026. The records do not say what prompted the scan, so ask your doctor if you want to know more about why it was done or about the spine changes.
